name: Aaron Pico
summary: Former Bellator blue-chipper (14-5, 1-1 UFC) who pairs an Olympic-trials freestyle wrestling base with fast, heavy boxing. Rebounded from a first-round spinning-elbow KO by Lerone Murphy in his UFC debut with a clear decision over Patricio Pitbull (30-27, 30-27, 29-28). Wins by front-loading violence, but all five of his losses are early stoppages.

how_they_fight.Striking: Fast, compact boxer (former Junior Golden Gloves) who throws looping hooks, uppercuts and hard body shots in combination; against Pitbull he rocked him with a left in round two and out-landed him 100 to 49 significant strikes. Entries are explosive but can be lunging: Cageside Press noted he took too many lunging shots and was out of position at times.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Elite freestyle wrestler (2nd at the 2016 U.S. Olympic Trials) who mixes reactive double-legs into his striking: 6 of 13 takedowns and about 3.5 minutes of control vs Pitbull, with elbows from top. Uses takedowns to bank rounds rather than to hunt submissions (2 career subs).
how_they_fight.Defense: The weak spot. Hittable when walking forward: Murphy caught him with a spinning back elbow while he pressed at 3:21 of R1; earlier KO losses to Henry Corrales (R1), Adam Borics (R2) and Jeremy Kennedy (end of R1). Pitbull's low kicks troubled and tripped him early at UFC 327.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Fast starter: 7 of his 11 finishes came in round one (6 KO, 1 sub), 2 in R2 and 2 in R3 (Aiden Lee sub, Adli Edwards TKO); 3 decisions. Showed he can go 15 minutes and finish strong vs Pitbull (late takedown, body work in R3). When he loses it is early: 4 of 5 losses in R1, one in R2 (Borics); he has never lost a decision.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Improved discipline: refused Pitbull's invitation to brawl late and coasted on a lead. Still prone to over-aggression in exchanges, which is exactly how Murphy and earlier Bellator opponents caught him.

patterns: Starts fast: most finishes in R1, rarely needs the cards (3 of 14 wins by decision)
Strike-to-shot mixing: hooks and uppercuts, then reactive double-leg
Goes to the body in combinations, especially late
Losses are always early stoppages (4 in R1, 1 in R2); never lost a decision
Banks rounds with takedowns and top elbows when the knockout isn't there
concerns: Chin/defensive exposure when pressing forward (5 stoppage losses, incl. Murphy spinning elbow)
Lunging entries leave him out of position against counter-punchers
Leg kicks slowed him early vs Pitbull
keys_to_beat: Counter his forward entries, especially in round one
Chop the lead leg to blunt his blitz and level changes
Survive the first round and make him work from range

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 145.5 lb (Keita 146).
Sherdog preview: -115 (Keita -105); thinks he becomes hittable when he attacks and that 'old habits will resurface'; picks Keita by first-round KO.
Media day: says he has changed his mindset after the Murphy loss and wants to 'cook the fight a little' rather than rush the finish; no injury news.
Original opponent Arnold Allen withdrew (not fully healed from earlier treatment, per MMA Fighting via Cageside Press); Losene Keita steps in on about five weeks' notice.
Says he had expected to fight Aljamain Sterling next; Sterling later said he turned down the Pico fight at UFC 333.
Calls Keita a dangerous power puncher who 'swings really, really hard'; no injury or camp issues reported.
